variants.before: Original source, 95af680; perturber geometry stopped, adaptive controller differentiated.
variants.frozen-only: Original source, with stop_gradient on the supplied controller output (workaround B). Acceleration-time derivatives remain incorrect.
variants.no-stops: Remove stops on Newtonian perturber positions and PPN perturber positions/velocities only (fix A).
variants.combined: Final source: fix A and stop_gradient on the controller output inside ias15_step (fix B).

method.device: Local macOS ARM CPU; JAX 0.11.1, Python 3.13.11, float64.
method.workload: Synthetic NEO: a=2.08 au, e=0.5, i=8 deg, Omega=60 deg, omega=120 deg, nu=270 deg, epoch 2000-01-01 TDB. Default DE440 solar-system gravity plus A2=0.
method.sky_outputs: Tangent-plane offsets [arcsec] including light travel time, geocentric observer.
method.xyz_outputs: Barycentric position [km], no observer or light travel time.
method.sampling: One-year: days 30,100,200,365. Ten-year sparse: days 30,365,1461,3652. Ten-year dense: 256 equally spaced days from 30 to 3652.
method.synchronization: jax.block_until_ready on every execution. Separate processes for each variant, no concurrent benchmark or test processes.
method.compilation: Wall time of jax.jit(fn).lower(argument).compile(); ephemeris setup and nominal sky-reference calculation excluded. Warm execution reported separately.
method.accuracy: Central finite differences with h=1 and h=0.1 in the seven scaled parameter units. Column-relative L2 norms over all output epochs and axes. Small perturbations show roundoff; the regression tests also compare h=10 and h=1.
method.limitations: Single synthetic orbit and local CPU. Samples quantify within-process variation; run order and CPU-frequency drift limit interpretation of small percentage differences. No GPU, batched-particle, or close-encounter performance claim.
method.source_reproduction: Apply each run git_diff to git_head. frozen-only also requires --freeze-controller. Use the saved benchmark script for every variant.
method.integrator_configuration: IAS15 GLOBAL controller, default dense buffer max_steps=None (15000). Initial dt=0.001 day; sky path applies its standard light-travel-time seed floor. Default tolerances and gravity constants unchanged.

     is prone to.
 
     Supports forward-mode AD only (``jax.lax.while_loop`` has no reverse-mode rule).
-    Also, because the step sequence is chosen adaptively from the state, an
-    infinitesimal change in the initial state can change the realized number and
-    placement of steps: the outputs (and any scalar built from them, e.g. a
-    likelihood) are only piecewise-smooth in the initial state, with
-    discontinuities at roughly the integrator tolerance. Use forward-mode AD for
-    derivatives — it differentiates the realized step sequence and is exact for
-    the function actually evaluated. Finite differences straddle the
-    discontinuities and silently return garbage whenever the true derivative is
-    small (weakly-constrained directions).

+    sensitivities to integration accuracy, rather than the exact derivative of
+    every numerical choice made by the adaptive algorithm. The acceleration's
+    explicit time dependence must remain differentiable.
+
+    Finite differences can validate these sensitivities, but their perturbation
+    sizes must be checked for convergence: changes in the realized step sequence
+    and floating-point roundoff can dominate a small finite-difference signal.
 
     Args:
